extracted.intended_audience: new and mid-career local government managers, assistant managers, and career-changers new to local government
extracted.subtask_description: An on-demand professional certificate (Local Government 201) that takes learners beyond basics to provide practical, experience-focused understanding of key local government management areas, taught by seasoned practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication skills for working with staff, peers, and superiors
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication skills that will help you effectively work with your staff, peers, and superiors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn how to communicate up, down, across, and outside your organization. This course also teaches you practical methods for communicating with your council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for citizen engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on effective methods for engaging community members and stakeholders (listed as a core learning objective).

rubrics_metrics.name: Latest advancements in public safety
rubrics_metrics.description: The latest advancements in public safety
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers how technology, legislation, and social issues are changing delivery of fire, emergency medical, and police services; included in Course Two (Public Safety: Trends and Innovations...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Race and policing; promoting diversity, inclusion, and justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Race and policing in America, and how to promote diversity, inclusion, and justice within the ranks and in the community
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly addresses race in American public safety as part of Course Two; examines social issues and institutional practices to promote equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices in crisis communication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a distinct learning objective and as part of the Public Safety course content, emphasizing practical crisis messaging and response coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental, economic sustainability and social equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental sustainability, economic sustainability and social equity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course Three (Building Community) explores these three sustainability pillars and discusses how to develop a sustainability plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smart cities and planning for innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Smart cities and how to plan for innovation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers technologies and planning approaches for municipal innovation; included in Building Community course content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placemaking types and economic impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The four types of placemaking and how they can impact your local economy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course material discusses the four types of placemaking and their effects on local economic development and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational development and talent retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational development and how to attract and keep top talent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course Four covers alternative work models, succession planning, and strategies for becoming an employer of choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative work models and succession planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative work schedules to succession planning and becoming an employer of choice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific topics listed under Course Four that provide tactics and structures for workforce management and leadership continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership at all levels and building leadership teams
rubrics_metrics.description: What it takes to be a leader and how to infuse leadership into your organization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course Five explores leadership at all levels, how to create a true leadership team, and how to become an innovative leader (taught by ICMA's Felicia Logan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, experience-focused pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Move beyond theory and focus on sharing experiences of how the job actually gets done
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program emphasizes practical understanding delivered by seasoned local government managers and experts rather than purely theoretical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor qualifications: seasoned practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Taught by a team of seasoned local government managers and experts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor credibility is highlighted as part of program design and learning approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of LG 101 or 5 years of experience in local government management is a prerequisite for taking LG 201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollment is restricted to those who meet the prerequisite through prior course completion or demonstrable experience.
